title: Inside Kap's Cafe Dubai, Where Masala Chai Costs Rs 500
excerpt: Kapil Sharma's Al Karama cafe, themed on his Netflix show, sells pani puri for about Rs 800 and pasta for AED 62 — a premium take on Indian street food in Dubai.
body:
• Kap's Cafe, comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Dubai's Al Karama area near Zabeel Park, charges about Rs 500 for masala chai and Rs 800 for pani puri, according to The Indian Express.
  • The cafe opened on December 31, 2025, after the first Kap's Cafe in Surrey, Canada, and is themed on Sharma's Netflix series The Great Indian Kapil Show.
  • The menu mixes Indian street food with Western cafe dishes — the priciest item reported is Classic Penne at AED 62, with Tiramisu Toast and Alfredo Pasta at AED 60 each.
  • For visitors: budget roughly Rs 1,600 for two, and note the reported hours of 4 pm to midnight.

A cup of masala chai at Kapil Sharma's Dubai cafe costs about Rs 500. A plate of pani puri costs about Rs 800. Those two prices, reported by The Indian Express in an inside look at the cafe, explain why Kap's Cafe has drawn as much attention for its menu as for its owner.

Kap's Cafe is the Dubai outpost of the cafe brand Sharma runs with his wife, Ginni Chatrath. It opened on New Year's Eve, December 31, 2025, in Al Karama, near Zabeel Park, according to Dubai News. It is the brand's first outlet in the Middle East and its second outside India, after Surrey, Canada.

What Is on the Menu

The menu is a fusion of Indian street food and Western cafe fare. Pani puri sits alongside breakfast toasts, bowls, pastas and savoury appetisers. Dubai News reported that the most expensive item is the Classic Penne at AED 62, followed by Tiramisu Toast and Alfredo Pasta at AED 60 each. Other coverage of the cafe has highlighted pani puri served with avocado salsa, Schezwan noodles, an acai bowl, Kap's hot chocolate and a mango pina colada among its recommended items.

Drinks are central to the offer. Alongside speciality coffees, teas and matcha, the menu includes a jaggery-flavoured lime juice described in coverage of the launch as a personal favourite of Sharma's. That detail matters to the cafe's pitch: this is comfort food tied to the owner's own tastes, not a generic celebrity licence.

The Indian Express headline prices put the cafe firmly in Dubai's premium casual bracket. Masala chai and pani puri are inexpensive street items in India. In Al Karama, a neighbourhood known for far cheaper South Asian eateries, Kap's Cafe is selling the setting, the name and the experience as much as the food itself.

"Habibi, welcome to Kap's Cafe. Launching tomorrow in Dubai – 31st December."

— Kapil Sharma, announcing the launch on Instagram

A Cafe Built Like a Television Set

The interiors are pastel and deliberately photogenic. Dubai News described blush pinks, muted greens and neutral tones, plush seating, statement lighting, chandeliers and floral arrangements. A large pot of pastel pink roses and a vintage-style car outside carry the Kap's Cafe branding. The design draws directly on The Great Indian Kapil Show, Sharma's Netflix series, so fans walk into a space that looks like an extension of the programme.

Bollywood Hungama reported at the launch that Sharma announced the opening with a video opening on the Dubai skyline and zooming in on the cafe, where he is seen greeting a customer with a cup of coffee. Fellow comedians Bharti Singh and Kiku Sharda were among those who congratulated the couple. The same report noted the show's fourth season had recorded 2.3 million views in its first two weeks on Netflix India.

Why Dubai, and Why Now

Dubai is a logical second international step. The emirate has one of the world's largest Indian expatriate populations, a strong cafe culture, and a steady flow of Indian tourists for whom a visit to a television star's cafe is an outing in itself. For Sharma, the cafe converts a streaming audience into a physical business — one that keeps earning between seasons.

The expansion also follows a difficult year for the Canadian outlet, which was targeted in multiple firing incidents in 2025. Sharma continued with the Dubai opening regardless, and the new cafe has since drawn a stream of inside-look visits from Dubai-based creators, which is how the Indian Express price list reached a wider audience this week.

What It Costs a Visitor

For diaspora readers planning a visit, the practical numbers are these: expect about Rs 1,600 for two, according to one detailed cafe guide, with signature street-food items priced well above their equivalents elsewhere in Al Karama. Reported hours are 4 pm to midnight, Monday to Sunday. Go for the novelty, the photographs and the show connection — and order the chai knowing exactly what it costs.
